claims.text: The starting eutectic high-entropy alloy has a hierarchical microstructure consisting of dual-phase lamellar colonies.
A secondary precipitation treatment can introduce a controlled density of nanoscale precipitates within the lamellar colonies.
Introducing nanoscale precipitates can overcome limited room-temperature tensile ductility and brittleness while retaining or increasing strength.
The nanoscale precipitates act as obstacles to dislocation motion.
The precipitate obstacles reduce dislocation pile-ups near internal boundaries.
Reducing dislocation pile-ups decreases local stress concentrations.
Decreased local stress concentrations reduce microcracking during straining.
Decreased microcracking reduces catastrophic damage during straining.
The reduction in pile-ups and associated damage improves tensile ductility.
The nanoscale precipitates increase strength through precipitation hardening.
The treated alloy will exhibit a 20% increase in yield strength relative to the untreated alloy.
The treated alloy will exhibit a 50% increase in tensile ductility relative to the untreated alloy.
The proposed response applies under uniaxial tensile loading at 20°C and a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1.
The proposed operating load range is 0 to 1000 MPa.
The effectiveness of the precipitates depends on their size, distribution, and interaction with the existing microstructure.
The effectiveness of the treatment may vary with alloy composition and processing history.
